full_form: Hypernephroid tumor -> ICD-O-3.2 8311/1 [obs]; ICCC-3 Group VI admits behaviour 3 only on this stem, so no Group VI code is emitted
notes: This is the REDCap dropdown label still printed against option 8311, and it is not the same disease as what code 8311 now records. 'Hypernephroid tumor' is ICD-O-3.2's obsolete term for 8311/1, a borderline-behaviour renal tumour. Do not select REDCap option 8311 for a case described only this way. The current ICD-O-3.2 term on the 8311 stem, at behaviour 3, is Hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell carcinoma (HLRCC) syndrome-associated renal cell carcinoma, and Moch H, et al. European Urology 2022;82(5):458-468, Table 1 assigns seven distinct, molecularly defined renal cell carcinomas to that same stem - see the TFE3-rearranged, TFEB-altered, ELOC-mutated, fumarate hydratase-deficient, HLRCC, succinate dehydrogenase-deficient and eosinophilic solid and cystic entries, plus ALK-rearranged renal cell carcinoma. If the pathology report names one of those entities, or states one of their defining molecular findings, use that entry instead. No registrar ruling exists yet for where a genuine 8311/1 case should be recorded in this registry; flagged, not guessed, per the standing rule against fabricating a destination.

notes: One of seven molecularly defined renal cell carcinomas that ICD-O-3.2 groups under a single code, 8311/3, new in the 3.2 revision (IARC '3.1 to 3.2 -- New codes and their terms', p. 5). coding_note: ICD-O-3.2 Preferred term, exact match to the generated morphology_entries[] name for 8311, confirmed by direct query of icdo32.sqlite (contract §0.5). Moch H, et al. full_form: HLRCC -> Hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell carcinoma (HLRCC) syndrome-associated renal cell carcinoma (8311)
notes: The standard abbreviation for hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell carcinoma syndrome, used in genetics and pathology reports for both the syndrome and its associated kidney cancer. Recorded as 8311/3.
coding_note: Clinical abbreviation for the ICD-O-3.2 Preferred term on the 8311 stem (contract §0.5). Kept short deliberately: a genetics or molecular-pathology report is more likely to write the abbreviation than the full syndrome name.

full_form: MiT family translocation carcinoma -> Hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell carcinoma (HLRCC) syndrome-associated renal cell carcinoma (8311)
notes: The umbrella term for the TFE3-rearranged and TFEB-altered renal cell carcinomas together - the commonest renal cell carcinoma subtype in this age group, 41.5% of paediatric and young-adult renal cell carcinoma in the largest series (Cajaiba MM, et al. Cancer 2018;124(16):3381-3389, TFE3 93.2% of that 41.5%, TFEB 6.8%). Recorded as 8311/3. Use the 'TFE3-rearranged' or 'TFEB-altered' entry when the report names the specific rearrangement.
coding_note: ICD-O-3.2 Related term on the 8311/3 stem, confirmed by direct query of icdo32.sqlite (contract §0.5 database dump). Frequency figure and workup order (TFE3 immunohistochemistry, then TFE3/TFEB break-apart FISH, then fusion-specific FISH, then next-generation sequencing) from Cajaiba MM, et al. Cancer 2018;124(16):3381-3389, p. 3387: a negative break-apart FISH does not overturn a positive TFE3 immunohistochemistry, because NONO::TFE3 and RBM10::TFE3 rearrangements are inversions the probes can miss.

full_form: TFE3-rearranged -> Hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell carcinoma (HLRCC) syndrome-associated renal cell carcinoma (8311)
notes: One of the two rearrangements behind MiT family translocation carcinoma (the other is TFEB), and by itself the commonest renal cell carcinoma subtype in children (Cajaiba MM, et al. Cancer 2018;124(16):3381-3389). Recorded as 8311/3 on diffuse strong nuclear TFE3 immunohistochemistry with matching morphology, TFE3 break-apart FISH, or fusion-specific testing - immunohistochemistry alone is sufficient and does not require a positive FISH to confirm it.
coding_note: WHO 2022 entity name (Moch H, et al. European Urology 2022;82(5):458-468, Table 1), not itself a confirmed icdo32.sqlite row (unlike 'MiT family translocation carcinoma', its parent term, and 'Hereditary leiomyomatosis...', the stem's Preferred term) - origin_system set to Clinical descriptive term rather than ICD-O-3.2 to avoid overclaiming a database match this build did not verify.

full_form: TFEB-altered -> Hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell carcinoma (HLRCC) syndrome-associated renal cell carcinoma (8311)
notes: The rarer of the two MiT family translocation carcinoma rearrangements, about 6.8% of the translocation-carcinoma group (Cajaiba MM, et al. Cancer 2018;124(16):3381-3389). Recorded as 8311/3 on TFEB break-apart FISH or fusion-specific testing confirming the rearrangement.
coding_note: WHO 2022 entity name (Moch H, et al. European Urology 2022;82(5):458-468, Table 1), same provenance note as 'TFE3-rearranged'.

full_form: FH-deficient -> Hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell carcinoma (HLRCC) syndrome-associated renal cell carcinoma (8311)
